name: Kaziranga National Park
blurb: Floodplain elephant grass, one-horned rhinos and tigers on the Brahmaputra.

tip.title: Hold back the flood
tip.text: Floods bring silt and fresh grass but also push animals to higher ground. Set Brahmaputra floods to -100% and watch the grasses, then the grazers and the tiger.

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Kaziranga National Park, Indian rhinoceros, Tiger). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: A short creeping grass that Wikipedia lists among the main foods of the Indian rhinoceros and the wild water buffalo.
Floating and submerged plants of the beels, or flood lakes. Rhinos eat them, but invasive water hyacinth can choke the water bodies.
A grazer of grasses that also eats leaves, fruit and aquatic plants. Over 70% of the species lives at Kaziranga, and tigers sometimes take unguarded calves.
Eats grasses and fruit, with GloBI records for elephant apple. Tigers have been recorded taking calves.
The most recorded deer near the park. It lives in the tall grass and is taken by tigers, jungle cats and pythons in GloBI records.
An omnivore that roots for plant foods in the grassland and woodland, and is itself prey for tigers.

nodes.name: Freshwater fish
nodes.desc: About 42 fish species live in the area. Many graze plants and small animals of the rivers and beels, and feed otters, eagles and storks.

nodes.name: Bengal tiger
nodes.desc: The top predator. It hunts deer, wild boar and buffalo, and rarely takes young elephants or rhinos.
Warm sunny months drive fast regrowth of the grasses.
June to September rains bring most of the year's water to the park.

nodes.name: Fungi & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead grass and carcasses and return nutrients to the floodplain soil.

story: Kaziranga National Park in Assam, India, lies on the edge of the Brahmaputra River. Dense tropical broadleaf forest is mixed with tall elephant grass and marsh around many beels. It hosts Indian rhinoceros, Asian elephant, wild water buffalo, swamp deer, tiger and fishing cat.
matters: It is an Important Bird Area and a Tiger Reserve since 2006. It began as a reserve forest in 1905, created to protect the dwindling Indian rhinoceros.
